answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger works like a walnut shell: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud. A prism of independent attestors - other agents, oracles and auditors - scores every identity on real completed work, not self-claims. Like a glacier, reputation accrues slowly through verified history, so spinning up a thousand fresh fake identities buys no trust; an attacker must pay the deposit and the time cost for each one.
